claim: TinyCNN's 16-bit fixed-point exclusive-mode FPGA accelerator achieves 15.75x speedup over 32-bit floating-point software on ARM, with only ~3% accuracy loss.
stance_target: tiny CNN accelerators on embedded FPGAs can match near-software accuracy with large speedups, a viable undergraduate novelty angle
scope_conditions: PYNQ board, Xilinx Zynq-7000 XC7Z020, CIFAR-10 grayscale, small 4-conv-layer CNN (292,566 params)
quoted_support: We used 16-bit fixed-point data in a CNN accelerator (FPGA) and compared it to the exactly similar software version running on an ARM processor (32-bit floating point data). We encounter about 3% accuracy loss in classification of the accelerated (FPGA) version. In return, we got up to 15.75x speedup

claim: Software CIFAR-10 classification (32-bit float, ARM 650MHz) achieves 65.54% accuracy at 42.54 ms/image, versus 62.28% accuracy at 2.7 ms/image for the exclusive-mode 16-bit fixed-point FPGA hardware accelerator.
stance_target: quantified accuracy/latency tradeoff table for CNN-on-FPGA projects

claim: TinyCNN's automated hardware backend uses CHISEL to generate configurable, modular convolution units that can run in resource-saving 'shared' mode or higher-throughput 'exclusive' mode.
stance_target: methodological design choice available for undergraduate replication
scope_conditions: framework design, not a specific numeric result
quoted_support: Shared mode: in the this mode, the convolution unit is shared among all layers of CNN... Exclusive mode: in the exclusive mode, for each convolution layer in the CNN a convolution unit hardware is generated, which results in higher throughput and FPGA resource usage.

claim: On-chip BRAM memory, not compute, is the binding hardware resource limitation for CNN accelerators on embedded FPGAs.
stance_target: memory (not LUT/DSP) is often the practical constraint for student CNN-on-FPGA projects targeting small boards
quoted_support: As we expected, memory (BRAM) is the hardware resource limitation that we encounter while implementing a CNN on an embedded FPGA.
